open_points.subject: scratch-file limit source
open_points.text: “ResourceBounds M04 are enforced with `setrlimit` (address space, each scratch file's size, processes)” conflicts with M04, whose only fields are `wall_time_ms`, `memory_bytes`, `output_bytes`, and `process_count`, while rule 1 separately names `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`.
open_points.question: Which value is installed as the per-file scratch limit?
options: `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`
the contract's `output_bytes`
a new ResourceBounds field

open_points.subject: process-count enforcement
open_points.text: “processes” does not say whether `process_count` includes the sandbox runner or only processes available to agent code.
open_points.question: What exact `setrlimit` value and counting rule implements a contract's `process_count`?
options: set the limit to `process_count + 1` so the runner is excluded
set the limit to `process_count`, including the runner
count only child processes by another mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Set the limit to `process_count + 1`, treating `process_count` as the processes available to the implementation.

open_points.subject: sandbox process capabilities
open_points.text: “set inside the environment before the code loads and beyond the code's power to raise” fixes only the limits; it no longer says whether the agent process has Linux capabilities or whether bubblewrap capability defaults may be overridden.
open_points.question: Which Linux capabilities, if any, may the runner and agent-written code retain inside the sandbox?
options: no capabilities, and bubblewrap's unprivileged default is never overridden
a fixed capability allow-list
whatever capabilities bubblewrap or the host supplies
open_points.default_guess: Run with no capabilities and never override bubblewrap to add any.

open_points.subject: scratch-limit hit classification
open_points.text: “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`” does not define whether an attempted write past the file-size limit counts when it returns a short write or error that the implementation catches, or when the implementation changes the file-size signal disposition.
open_points.question: Exactly which observable file-write events constitute a scratch-limit hit, and do they force `resource_exhausted` even when `run` catches the error and returns conforming outputs?
options: every kernel refusal, short write, or file-size signal caused by the configured limit counts and forces `resource_exhausted`
only termination by the file-size signal counts; caught write failures remain the code's result
only an uncaught write failure or abnormal exit counts
open_points.default_guess: Treat every write attempt rejected because of the configured file-size limit as `resource_exhausted`, even if caught.

open_points.subject: host storage exhaustion
open_points.text: The text says a scratch limit hit is `resource_exhausted` but is silent on a scratch write failing because host storage, inode capacity, or quota is exhausted rather than because the configured file-size limit was reached.
open_points.question: How is host-storage exhaustion during a sandbox scratch write classified, including when the implementation catches the write error?
options: an ordinary Python write error: success remains possible if caught, otherwise `crashed`
`resource_exhausted` in every case
`internal_error` or `stop_required` because the host cannot provide the sandbox
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an ordinary Python write error, yielding `crashed` only if it escapes `run`.

open_points.subject: aggregate scratch usage
open_points.text: “each scratch file's size” fixes a per-file limit but does not say whether the exchange directory also has an aggregate byte, block, inode, or file-count limit.
open_points.question: May an execution create arbitrarily many individually compliant scratch files up to host capacity, or is there a separate aggregate scratch-directory limit; if so, what is its value and accounting rule?
options: no separate aggregate limit in this release
the whole directory is limited to `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`
a separate release ceiling limits aggregate bytes and/or file count
open_points.default_guess: Provide no separate aggregate scratch-directory limit.

open_points.subject: sandbox start probe
open_points.text: Rule 8 requires “one probe execution succeeds,” while the deleted text was the only passage saying that the probe runs the same runner with current ceilings; `probe_sandbox` takes no ResourceBounds input.
open_points.question: Which resource bounds and scratch ceiling must the start probe install, and therefore which inability to set a limit prevents the kernel from starting?
options: all current release ceilings
a fixed minimal probe-specific set of bounds
representative bounds chosen by the sandbox implementation
no resource limits during the probe
open_points.default_guess: Run the probe with all current release ceilings and fail start if any cannot be installed.
